title: Investigate and remediate KEDA/HPA mis-scaling during bursty inference load (postmortem & action items)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Postmortem and follow-up work for a capacity/regression event where KEDA and HPA produced aggressive scale-ups and scale-downs during bursty inference traffic, causing elevated latency and client errors for ~3 hours. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, decisions, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2025-11-06 09:10 UTC - Spike detection: internal SLO alerts triggered for 95p latency on inference-hosted cluster
2025-11-06 09:12 UTC - KEDA scaler logs show multiple rapid ScaleUp events (pods +40% over 7 minutes).
2025-11-06 09:15 UTC - Autoscaler (ClusterAutoscaler + provider) began provisioning new GPU-backed nodes (image pull delays observed).
2025-11-06 09:22 UTC - Several new pods failed readiness due to KV cache warmup delay and readinessProbe gating; traffic routed prematurely to partially warmed replicas.
2025-11-06 09:25 UTC - Error budget burn: client 5xx errors and timeouts climb. On-call engaged and applied emergency mitigation: increased KEDA scalingCooldownSeconds and temporarily raised HPA target thresholds (09:34 UTC).
2025-11-06 11:45 UTC - Traffic returned to normal after scale and routing stabilization; incident declared mitigated.
2025-11-07 10:00 UTC - Initial postmortem drafted and cross-team review started.
2025-11-12 15:20 UTC - Postmortem review meeting: product and infra agreed on prioritized action items.
impact: ~3 hours elevated latency and ~12% increase in 5xxs across hosted inference endpoints for a subset of customers. Estimated customer-facing requests affected: ~120K. Operational cost spike from over-provisioned nodes during the event estimated at +18% for the 3-hour window.
root_cause: Multi-factor: (1) KEDA external scaler observed short-lived metric spikes from a Prometheus exporter that reported bursty queue_length due to a recent instrumentation change; the scaler's aggregation window was too short and reacted to transient spikes (false positives). (2) HPA target and KEDA thresholds were not aligned for GPU-backed workloads: scale-up was aggressive while scale-down cooldowns were too low. (3) New pods require a non-trivial KV cache warmup for serving quality — readiness gating was superficially configured so some replicas were marked ready before warm cache, leading to increased tail latency. (4) Node provisioning and container image pull latency amplified the impact because scale-up timing assumed faster warm-starts.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Use longer aggregation/stabilization windows to reduce false positive scale-ups at the cost of slightly slower reaction to real sustained load increases.
- Implement a warm-pool (pre-warmed replicas) for critical GPU-backed inference routes to reduce cold-start latency; tradeoff is baseline resource cost.
- Avoid scale-to-zero for high-SLO endpoints unless backed by pre-warm capacity.
- Add adaptive scale-up policies that consider both external metrics and pod readiness fraction to avoid routing to under-warmed replicas.
action_items: Increase KEDA ScaledObject stabilizationWindowSeconds from 15s to 90s for queue-length scalers on gpu inference clusters — owner: Liam O'Connor — due: 2025-11-20
Introduce a moving-average smoothing pipeline for external metrics in Prometheus (recording rule) and update scaler to read smoothed metric — owner: Priya Rao — due: 2025-11-25
Implement 'warm pool' of pre-warmed GPU pods for top 10% latency-sensitive routes (config flag + rollout) — owner: Marco Diaz — due: 2025-12-01, estimate: 8
Adjust HPA target CPU and custom metrics alignment with KEDA thresholds; publish a documented tuning guide for GPU-backed services — owner: Aisha Patel — due: 2025-11-28
Enhance readinessProbe logic so pods only become Ready after KV cache warmup or a warmup probe passes; add readiness gating to the load-balancer routing — owner: Sasha Ivanov — due: 2025-11-22
Add Prometheus alerts for rapid transient spikes (spike_count > 3 within 60s) and KEDA scaler anomaly alerts to PagerDuty — owner: Ops Team (on-call rota) — due: 2025-11-18
Create a retro runbook and a Confluence checklist for KEDA/HPA incidents, include rollback steps and emergency knob values — owner: Liam O'Connor — due: 2025-11-19
verification_plan: 1) Deploy KEDA stabilization config to staging and run synthetic burst tests simulating Prometheus spike patterns; verify no unnecessary scale-ups. 2) Validate warm-pool reduces 95p latency for cold-start scenarios by >60%. 3) Run chaos test where metrics emitter misreports to ensure smoothing prevents flapping. 4) Verify alerts fire for true sustained load but not for single short spikes.
notes:
- During the incident we discovered a concurrent instrumentation change in the metrics exporter (PR #8942) that reduced push frequency and caused transient aggregation artifacts. PR link listed below.
- Design/PM feedback in review: product asked that top-tier customers have opt-in pre-warm defaults.
- Ops requested adding a visible 'warm pool' cost line in the Console cost breakdown dashboard for transparency.
